full_judgment:
3. The case of the plaintiff is, in brief, that the former Jaminder Moharaja Shashikanto Acharya Chowdhury was the owner of the suit land under whom Ram Sundar Dutta was tenant. Ram Sunder Dutta died leaving behind two sons, namely Satish Chandra Dutta and Romesh Chandra Dutta. Satish Chandra Dutta and Ram Chandra Dutta settled the suit land with Jan Mahmud Sheikh, Enam Box Bepari and Mirajuddin Sheikh. The CS Khatian was prepared accordingly. Out of the suit land, the land of plot No. 1073 was recorded in the name of Jan Mahmud and the land of plot Nos. 1070 and 1975 were recorded in the names of Enam Box Bepari and Mirajuddin. Jan Mahmud surrendered his land to the landlord. Thereafter, the plaintiff's father took settlement of the said land from the landlords, since such settlement he had been enjoying and possessing the same by paying rent to the landlords. While the said landlords expressed their wish to sell the suit property, the father of the plaintiff expressed his interest to purchase that land, but ultimately the land was not sold to them. The father of the plaintiff converted the suit land into a pond and had been enjoying and possessing the pond by rearing fishes therein. By operation of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1951 plaintiff's father acquired title in the suit land. During settlement survey the government officials assured him that the suit land would be recorded properly in his name in the SA Khatian. His father transferred the suit land to the plaintiff by way of oral gift and since then he has been enjoying and possessing the same. With an intention to mortgage the suit land with the bank to get loan he went to the local Tahshil office wherefrom he came to know the suit land was recorded as khas property of the government though he has been enjoying and possessing the same, and hence the suit. 

 4. The defendant-government contested the suit by filing written statement denying the claims of the plaintiff stating that the suit land has been properly recorded as Government's khas land and the plaintiff has got no right, title and possession over the suit land. 

 9. Heard the learned Advocate and perused the impugned order and the application upon which the impugned order was passed which is annexed to the revisional application as Annexure-A. On perusal of the said application, it appears that as per the statements made in the said application, on 18-1-2000 the witnesses were examined on behalf of the review petitioner in the review case and one witness namely, Md Abdur Rahim Tashilder of Mymensingh Town, submits some certified copies of some khatians and the volume books, but those were not marked as exhibits, as such, those required to be marked as exhibits. The learned Joint District Judge rejected the said application on the finding that, in the review matter the cardinal principle followed is that the alleged discovery of new and important matter or mistake or error should be determined without entertaining the elaborate argument of the party concerned rather it should be apparent on the face of the record. He holds the view that his predecessor recorded the deposition of PWs in the review proceeding on misconception of law and the documents submitted by the review petitioner need not be marked as exhibits on the basis of oral evidence. The government can conduct the hearing of the Review Case on the basis of these documents and satisfy the court about its discovery, realising the alleged mistake of the court on misconception of law he found no necessity to mark those documents as exhibits. On perusal of the said order it appears that the learned Joint District Judge himself is doubtful that whether the Review Case itself is maintainable or not. With such confusion he rejected the prayer of the Review Case by the impugned order. However, the learned Advocate of the opposite party submits further that the Review Petition itself is not maintainable. The question of maintainability of any proceeding pending before any court subordinate to this court can be decided by this Court even 'suo moto'. In the instant case, the suit was decreed by the trial Court and such decree was affirmed by the appellate Court also. The judgment-debtor defendant has got ample scope to file revision before this division if he feels aggrieved with the judgment of the appellate Court, but without filing any revisional application the defendant filed the Review Case in a manner which is apparently not legal, and it is also apparent from the application (Annexure-A to the revisional application) that the learned Joint District Judge had been proceeding with the Review Case in an illegal manner. On perusal of the decisions cited above, I hold the view that the review petition which is numbered as a Miscellaneous Review Case itself is not maintainable and I find no illegality with the impugned order.
